The rule-versus-observation test decided every prose edit: version.go's contract history and the CHANGELOGs record what a numbered contract changed and stay; a sentence telling a reader what a deployment must name is the defect.

Stage 4a's inverted checks are still unrun; the runner's revised list, marking each of 65 rows changed or unchanged, is a comment on the pull request.
The branch was 9 behind main within a minute of the push, with no conflict. The two lanes at this head were still queued when the round completed; the daemon reads their settlement.
discoveredComplexity: A merge generalises a rule and leaves its machinery behind. The configuration rule became 'a store that keeps sessions in a database' while two launch paths kept 'the store is postgres', and the failure landed on the daemon's boot rather than on a pod. The search that finds this is not 'what did the merge touch' but 'what reasons from the old premise'.

The text a merge cannot touch is the text that rots. docs/kubernetes.md survived because it was one of the fourteen conflicted files and every sentence was read against both sides; the pull request body, the site page and the file an operator copies were reached by no diff and kept the pre-merge rule.

Hardening creates new failure modes in its own right. Round 4's refusal was correct and made a new worst case reachable — every transcript lost, run green — which the hardening's author is the least likely reader to see, because it is read as a fix to something already reviewed.
